title: BYD Sells a Record 256,230 Battery-Electric Vehicles in a Single Month
detail: BYD reported August 2026 sales of 440,293 new-energy vehicles (NEVs), up 17.84% year-on-year and its highest monthly total of the year, driven by a record 256,230 passenger battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) sold -- the first time the company has topped 250,000 BEVs in a single month, up 28.4% YoY and 9.9% versus July. Overseas sales hit a fresh record of 189,466 units, up 134.45% YoY and now 43% of total NEV volume, even as domestic China sales fell 14.34% YoY to 250,827 units. BEVs made up 59.1% of passenger NEV sales, up from 53.7% a year earlier, reflecting a broader shift toward fully electric models as the world's largest EV maker leans on overseas demand to offset a soft domestic market.

media.caption: BYD sold a record 256,230 battery-electric vehicles in August 2026, its first month above 250,000 BEVs

title: China's Solar Power Capacity Surpasses Coal for the First Time in History
detail: China's National Energy Administration announced September 1, 2026 that cumulative installed photovoltaic capacity reached 1.286 TW (704 GW utility-scale + 582 GW distributed) at the end of July 2026, edging past the country's 1.285 TW of coal-fired capacity for the first time -- ending a century-long stretch in which coal was China's largest power source by installed capacity. Solar now accounts for roughly 31.5% of China's total installed generating capacity. China Electricity Council deputy director Liu Zhiqiang called it 'a milestone event in China's green and low-carbon energy transition,' while cautioning that coal will remain important for grid stability, since coal plants run at roughly 50% capacity factor versus about 14% for solar.

media.caption: China's installed solar power capacity has overtaken coal-fired capacity for the first time, NEA data shows

title: Norway's New-Car Market Hits World-Record 98.7% Electric Share
detail: Norway's Road Traffic Information Council (OFV) reported that battery-electric vehicles reached 98.7% of new passenger car registrations in August 2026 -- the highest EV market share ever recorded in any significant automotive market -- up from 96.9% a year earlier. Of 13,451 new cars registered, only 30 were gasoline and 64 diesel. The record came even as Norway's EV purchase incentives were trimmed during the year, and as the country's EV fleet passed one million vehicles. Volkswagen led August brand rankings (10.8% share, ID.4 the top-selling model) ahead of Toyota, while Chinese brands Xpeng and BYD together more than doubled their combined share year-on-year to 11.4%. Electric vans also hit a record 44.9% share of the month's van registrations.

media.caption: The VW ID.4 was Norway's top-selling car as EVs hit a record 98.7% market share in August 2026
